title: Sum of Two Integers
description:
Compute `a + b` for two integers **without using the `+` or `-` operators** anywhere in your code. Both inputs may be negative and lie within the 32-bit signed range.

Return the sum as a normal (possibly negative) integer.
hints: Adding two bits without carry is XOR. The carry out of each position is AND, shifted left by one.
Repeat: sum_without_carry = a ^ b, carry = (a & b) << 1; set a, b to those and loop until the carry is zero.

Python integers have no fixed width, so a negative carry never reaches zero. Mask every intermediate value with 0xFFFFFFFF to simulate 32 bits, then convert the final result back to a signed value if its top bit is set.
signature: def getSum(self, a: int, b: int) -> int:
approach:
**Key insight: a full adder is XOR for the sum bit and AND for the carry bit. Adding two numbers is repeatedly combining `a ^ b` (the digits) with `(a & b) << 1` (the carries) until no carry remains.**

Loop: `carry = (a & b) << 1`, `a = a ^ b`, `b = carry`. Each round pushes the carries one position left, so after at most 32 rounds (the word width) the carry is zero and `a` is the sum.

**The Python wrinkle:** Python ints are unbounded, so for negative operands the carry's sign bits propagate forever and the loop never ends. Mask `a`, `b` and `carry` with `0xFFFFFFFF` to emulate a 32-bit register. At the end `a` is an unsigned bit pattern; if it exceeds `0x7FFFFFFF` it represents a negative number, which we recover with `~(a ^ MASK)` (flip the bits within 32 positions, then apply bitwise NOT, which is `-x - 1` without writing a minus sign).

**Why it is correct:** in two's complement, addition is the same bit operation for signed and unsigned values; only the interpretation of the top bit differs. So computing the unsigned 32-bit sum and reinterpreting it is exactly what hardware does.

**Common mistakes:** forgetting to mask the carry (infinite loop on negatives); converting with `a - 2**32`, which uses the forbidden minus; swapping the roles of `a` and `b` in the loop and losing the carry; stopping after one round instead of iterating until the carry is zero.

**Interview follow-ups:** (1) Subtraction: `a + (~b + 1)`, with the same adder. (2) Multiplication with only shifts and adds (Russian peasant). (3) Why the loop is bounded by the word width (each round the lowest set carry bit moves strictly left).
